[**Geology and Environmental Sciences**](https://xtec.gencat.cat/web/.content/curriculum/batxillerat/curriculum-171-2022/materias-de-modalitat/modalitat-ciencies-i-tecnologia/Geologia-i-Ciencies-Ambientals.pdf){target="_blank"}

The advances of humanity have often been based on the use of natural resources for the production of products or objects that solve existing problems or provide us with certain services. Among these resources, geological resources stand out, although often in an inconspicuous way. On the other hand, humans, as the inhabitants of the Earth that we are, are continuously exposed to geodynamic processes, which bring risks but also opportunities. In this sense, the analysis of the main events that have taken place in the history of our planet allows us to make predictions about current or future events to which we may be exposed.

The understanding of terrestrial dynamics and the knowledge of geological resources and, in particular, of their renewal rate, are aspects that make it possible to argue scientifically for the adoption of attitudes and habits compatible with the model of sustainable development. This type of action is and will be key to being able to deal with environmental impacts derived from human activities, some of which are as global and serious as the current climate emergency resulting from the increase in the greenhouse effect. On the other hand, the growing occupation of territory by our species and the increase in some natural risks derived from global warming, also imply the need to know the dynamics of these risks in order to make predictions about them that allow us to take actions to minimize our exposure.

The subject of Geology and Environmental Sciences aims to provide students who take it with the knowledge and skills necessary to understand the structure and dynamics of our planet and the phenomena that arise from it. These contents are treated with a global vision, integrating the interrelationships that occur with human activities, to allow students to have a critical view of the exploitation of natural resources and the resulting environmental impacts, as well as the natural risks that terrestrial dynamics imply for humans. For all this, this subject is based on specific skills that can be summarized as: interpreting and transmitting scientific information and arguing about its contents; locate, select and compare scientific information; design research papers and critically analyze their conclusions; pose and solve questions and problems related to geology and environmental sciences; analyze the environmental impacts of human activities to design actions and adopt habits compatible with sustainable development; analyze geological elements of the relief to explain its dynamics and origin, and be able to make predictions about natural risks to adopt attitudes to minimize our exposure.

The subject of Geology and Environmental Sciences must enable students to effectively manage information in the processes of selection, reworking and construction of knowledge, as well as in the formulation of questions and problems about processes and phenomena that occur in the Earth system and in their reasoned response. The approach adopted must enable students to apply the knowledge developed in an integrated way either in the production of texts that respond to a specific format and situation or in the design of contextualized experimental or field research in geology or environmental sciences, applied to the verification of a hypothesis or the development of solutions to problems applied in various contexts related to the subject. In the same way, the subject must make it possible for students to apply the learning developed to argue, with scientific, logical and ethical criteria, what uses should be made of natural resources in the future to minimize the resulting environmental impacts and, as a conclusion, propose and adopt habits and attitudes compatible with a model of sustainable development.

Competences must be worked on from learning situations, in real or meaningful contexts, that invite students to reflect, collaborate and take action.

The achievement of the specific skills constitutes the basis for the student's competence assessment and will be assessed through the assessment criteria. There is no univocal and direct link between assessment criteria and knowledge. Specific skills will be assessed by putting different knowledge into action, in different situations, providing the necessary flexibility to establish connections with each other. In a competence approach, the evaluation criteria and knowledge are organized around specific competences.

Accompanying the specific skills of this subject are the evaluation criteria. They are directly linked to the specific skills, they explain the assessment of the skills and knowledge that needs to be developed, they measure the degree of development of these skills and specify the learning we want to identify in the students and the way to do it. Their character is markedly competitive and makes them evaluators not only of theoretical content, but also of the skills and attitudes that students must acquire in order to develop in a society that demands a critical spirit both in the face of scientific questions and others of a social nature, where science plays an important role. The teaching staff must contextualize and make these criteria more flexible in accordance with the circumstances of their activity.

The development of the specific competences in Geology and Environmental Sciences is based on the key competences and knowledge of the subject, which are structured in five blocks in each course, which include essential knowledge, skills and attitudes. For this reason, it is chosen to formulate the knowledge linked to a capacity and in a context in which they must be developed. The teaching staff can develop an alternative context, if they consider it appropriate.

It is worth noting the first-year *scientific project of geology or environmental sciences* blog, which deals with the basic aspects of general scientific activity but contextualized in the study of our planet: the use of scientific methodologies for the study of natural phenomena, experimentation -including the necessary laboratory and field instruments and procedures and their rules of use-, the appropriate use of scientific languages and mathematical tools relevant, etc. This blog seeks to develop practical skills useful for the rest of the blogs. Also in the first year, in the block *the Earth, a particular planet*, a characterization of the planet Earth, its geodynamics and that of its fluid envelopes (hydrosphere and atmosphere) is made, which must serve as a conceptual basis for other blocks in the first and second year. This same blog also analyzes the concepts derived from the interaction between the Earth's natural processes and human activities (risk, resource, impact, exposure, etc.). In the blocks *minerals, the components of rocks* and *igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks*, mineral and rock conceptual models are worked on, and their basic typologies, origins and identification are analysed. Emphasis is also placed on analyzing the uses of minerals and rocks in our daily lives. Finally, in the *history of the Earth and life* blog, an approach is taken to the study of the history of the Earth, based on knowledge of the main dating methods and the analysis of the most relevant biological and geological events, to correlate them with the current characteristics of our planet and the processes that take place there.

In the second year, *geological and environmental information* is the first block that must be dealt with in a transversal and contextualized manner throughout the other four blocks, on the sources and forms of representation of geological and environmental information and data. In the blocks *plate tectonics and internal geodynamics* and *external geological processes* internal and external geodynamic processes are reviewed, respectively, to analyze their influence on the relief and, in particular, their interaction with human activities to know, predict and prevent the risks they generate. The blog *the fluid layers of the Earth* focuses on the dynamics of the Earth's fluid envelopes (hydrosphere and atmosphere), to assess the availability of the resources they provide us; identify, predict and prevent the risks they generate, as well as analyze the environmental impacts that human activities produce there, and argue actions to minimize them. The last block, *natural resources and sustainable management*, is the most extensive but also the most relevant, given that it focuses on the goals for sustainable development at the global level. Based on the analysis of the use we make of natural resources in our daily lives and the impacts that this use and their exploitation generate, the students will evaluate the preventive, corrective and compensatory measures necessary to minimize or reverse these impacts. They will also argue the need to adopt habits and attitudes that really lead us towards a model of sustainable development. Within this entire conceptual framework, which integrates many of the essential contents of other blogs, the soil as a resource and the problem of environmental impacts generated by waste and, in particular, the measures to minimize them, are also dealt with in a specific way.

Globally, the Geology and Environmental Sciences curriculum has the key objective of giving students the tools to know, interpret and act responsibly on our planet to preserve its diversity and richness. To achieve this, the proposed methodology is the use of learning situations contextualized in the numerous interactions that exist between the dynamics of the different elements that make up the Earth system (geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, etc.) and human activities. In short, the subject of Geology and Environmental Sciences provides students with the essential knowledge and skills to make decisions and act in relation to the environment and our interaction with it, with a critical approach that allows us to minimize our exposure to risks as well as the impacts that our activities can cause.

**Specific skills**

**Competition 1**

**Interpret, communicate and argue information and data from scientific works, accurately and using different formats, to analyze processes, methods, experiments or results of the geological and environmental sciences.**

**Evaluation criteria**

| 1st year | 2nd year |
| --- | --- |
| 1.1 Critically analyze concepts and processes in the subject of Geology and Environmental Sciences by selecting and interpreting information in different formats (maps, models, graphical sections, tables, etc.).  1.2 Communicate information or reasoned opinions on geology and environmental science topics, transmitting them clearly and rigorously, using the appropriate terminology and format (maps, models, graphs, tables, reports, diagrams, formulas, digital content, etc.) and responding in a well-founded manner to questions that may arise during the exhibition.  1.3 Have scientific discussions on aspects related to the knowledge of geology and environmental sciences, rationally considering the strengths and weaknesses of different positions and with a receptive and respectful attitude towards the opinion of others. | 1.1 Critically analyze concepts and processes in the subject of Geology and Environmental Sciences by interpreting information in different formats (models, graphs, tables, diagrams, formulas, diagrams, etc.).  1.2 Communicate information or reasoned opinions on geology and environmental science topics, transmitting them clearly and rigorously, using the appropriate terminology and format (models, graphs, tables, reports, diagrams, formulas, etc.) and digital tools, responding in a well-founded manner to questions that may arise during the exhibition.  1.3 Argue about situations related to geology and environmental sciences defending a scientifically reasoned position and with an open, flexible, receptive and respectful attitude towards the opinion of others. |

In the geological and environmental sciences, as in all other scientific disciplines, communication is an essential aspect of scientific progress, since advances and discoveries are rarely the product of the work of isolated individuals, but of collaborative teams, often of an interdisciplinary nature, in which the communication of information and data is key. In addition, knowledge creation only occurs when findings are published, allowing them to be reviewed and expanded by the scientific community and used to improve society.

In the case of geological and environmental sciences there are particular formats for the communication of data and information, such as maps (topographic, hydrographic, geological, vegetation, etc.), sections, flow diagrams or others. The development of this specific competence allows students to become familiar with these formats and acquire a complete view of the concepts, processes and phenomena related to the geological and environmental sciences and transmit them precisely and clearly. In this way, students will develop the necessary skills to extract the most relevant ideas from scientific information (in the form of articles, diagrams, tables, graphs, etc.) and communicate them in a simple, precise and truthful way, using varied formats (oral presentation, virtual platforms, slide presentation and poster, among others), both analog and digital.

In the same way, this specific competence seeks to enhance argumentation, understood as a communication process based on reasoning and evidence, essential for the social and professional development of students. Argumentation in debates, forums or other ways gives the opportunity to defend, in a logical and well-founded way, one's own positions, but also to understand and assimilate the ideas of other people. Argumentation is a form of collective thinking that enriches those who participate, and allows developing resilience in the face of challenges as well as the flexibility to change one's own ideas in the face of other people's arguments. Likewise, argumentation, done correctly, promotes tolerance and respect for diversity between individuals.

**Competition 2**

**Identify, select, organize and critically evaluate information, contrasting its reliability to solve questions posed autonomously and create content related to the geological and environmental sciences.**

**Evaluation criteria**

| 1st year | 2nd year |
| --- | --- |
| 2.1 Raise and solve questions related to geology and environmental sciences, locating and citing appropriate sources and selecting, organizing and critically analyzing information.  2.2 Contrast and justify the veracity of information related to geology and environmental sciences using reliable sources and adopting a critical and skeptical attitude towards information without a scientific basis.  2.3 Argue about the contribution of science to society and the work of the people who dedicate themselves to it, reflecting on gender bias in the sciences and understanding research as a collective and interdisciplinary task, in constant evolution and influenced by the political context and economic resources. | 2.1 Raise and resolve issues and create content related to geology and environmental sciences, locating and citing sources appropriately and selecting, organizing and critically analyzing information.  2.2 Contrast and justify the veracity of information related to geology and environmental sciences using reliable sources, providing data and adopting a critical and skeptical attitude towards information without a scientific basis. |

Obtaining relevant information in order to resolve doubts, acquire new knowledge or check the veracity of statements or news, is an essential skill for citizens of the 21st century. The collection and critical analysis of information are essential in making social decisions related to geology and the environment and in civic contexts such as democratic participation or lifelong learning. Likewise, all scientific research begins with the careful compilation, selection and critical evaluation of relevant publications in the area of ​​study.

Nowadays, through the Internet you can access many sources of information on any subject, including geology and environmental sciences. In this digital universe, reliable information coexists with conspiracy theories, incomplete or intentionally biased information and a whole string of pseudoscientific content.

Through the development of this competence, it is intended that students improve their skills to search and compare information from digital platforms or other formats, and develop a critical spirit to evaluate the information obtained. On the other hand, it also aims to be able to select truthful information according to its relevance and organize it to be able to respond clearly to the questions posed. In addition, given the intellectual maturity of students at this educational stage, it will encourage them to raise these questions out of their own curiosity and initiative.

Another aspect that promotes this specific competence is the subsequent creation of content based on the information collected and contrasted, which implies a higher degree of understanding of the information collected to be able to transmit it by structuring it in an original way, but maintaining rigor.

For these reasons, the development of this specific competence can have a very positive effect on the integration of students into today's society, which will facilitate their personal and professional growth and commitment as citizens.

**Competition 3**

**Design and develop geological and environmental science research projects and critically analyze the results, as well as those of research and dissemination work, checking if they follow the steps of scientific methodology to assess the reliability of the conclusions.**

**Evaluation criteria**

| 1st year | 2nd year |
| --- | --- |
| 3.1 Ask questions, make predictions and formulate hypotheses that can be answered or contrasted using scientific methods and try to explain geological and environmental phenomena.  3.2 Design experimentation and data collection for the analysis of geological and environmental phenomena, selecting the appropriate instruments to answer the research questions and contrast the hypotheses raised.  3.3 Carry out experiments and take quantitative and qualitative data on geological and environmental phenomena by selecting and using the appropriate instruments, tools or techniques with correctness and precision.  3.4 Interpret and analyze results obtained in research projects using, when necessary, mathematical and technological tools and recognizing their scope and limitations to obtain reasoned and grounded conclusions.  3.5 Establish collaborations inside and outside the educational center in the different phases of a scientific project to work more efficiently, using the appropriate technological tools, valuing the importance of cooperation in research, respecting diversity and promoting its inclusion.  3.6 Present clearly and rigorously the introduction, methodology, results and conclusions of a scientific project using the appropriate format and digital tools. | 3.1 Assess the reliability of the conclusions of research or scientific dissemination related to geology or environmental sciences based on the interpretation of the results obtained.  3.2 Argue, using concrete examples, about the contribution of science to society and the work of dedicated people, reflecting on gender bias in the sciences and understanding research as a collective and interdisciplinary task in constant evolution influenced by political and economic contexts. |

Scientific knowledge is built from evidence obtained from objective observation and experimentation. Its purpose is to explain the functioning of the world around us and to provide solutions to the problems of our time. Scientific methods are based on the formulation of researchable questions about the natural or social environment, the design and execution of appropriate strategies to be able to answer them, the interpretation and analysis of the results, the obtaining of conclusions and the communication of these. On the other hand, the pseudoscientific ideas, unfortunately more and more widespread, which have been generated without any validation process or have any objective evidence to support them, are very different.

Setting up situations in which students have the opportunity to develop this competence, applying the steps of the different methods used in science, contributes to developing their curiosity, critical sense, entrepreneurial spirit and skills for collaborative work. In addition, it makes it possible to understand the difference between an impression or opinion and evidence based on science, and to critically and judiciously assess the conclusions of scientific research works and information from popular documents. These skills are not only essential for a scientific career, but also for mobilizing critical thinking, logical reasoning and communication skills and using technological resources, thus promoting the integration and full participation of students as citizens. In addition, it allows the positive contribution of scientific work to society to be assessed.

**Competition 4**

**Apply learning in an integrated way and the various forms of reasoning typical of science, to pose and solve problems related to the geological and environmental sciences, looking for and using the appropriate strategies, critically analyzing the solutions and reformulating the procedure, if necessary.**

**Evaluation criteria**

| 1st year | 2nd year |
| --- | --- |
| 4.1 Solve problems to explain geological or environmental processes by searching and using various resources such as knowledge, data, information, reasoning or digital tools and resources.  4.2 Critically analyze the solution to problems on geological or environmental phenomena and modify the resolution procedures used or conclusions obtained if these were not viable or in the face of new data. | 4.1 Explain phenomena related to geology and environmental sciences through problem-solving and finding and using appropriate and diverse strategies and resources.  4.2 Critically analyze the solution to problems in geology or environmental sciences reformulating the procedures used or the conclusions obtained if these were not viable or in the face of new data. |

The use of reasoning is particularly important in the research of any scientific discipline to raise and contrast hypotheses and to face unforeseen events that hinder the progress of a project. Likewise, in various contexts of everyday life, it is necessary to use logical reasoning and other strategies to approach difficulties and solve problems of a different nature. People often face complex situations that require problem solving and the search for coherent explanations for different phenomena in the contexts of their daily lives.

The development of this specific competence involves working on four fundamental aspects: posing problems, using logical tools to solve them, searching for alternative resolution strategies if necessary and critically analyzing the validity of the solutions obtained. These four aspects require the mobilization of subject knowledge, skills such as logical reasoning, critical thinking and observation, and attitudes such as curiosity and resilience. The development of these skills and attitudes through this specific competence, allows to expand the personal and professional horizons of the students and their full integration as citizens committed to the improvement of society.

**Competition 5**

**Analyze the impacts of human activities on the environment or the availability of resources, based on field observations and information in different formats, to design, promote and execute environmental conservation initiatives and adopt habits compatible with sustainable development based on scientific foundations.**

**Evaluation criteria**

| 1st year | 2nd year |
| --- | --- |
| 5.1 Analyze from observations and scientific knowledge of geology and environmental sciences the causes and ecological, social and economic consequences of the main environmental problems from a personal, local and global perspective, conceiving them as great challenges for humanity.  5.2 Propose and justify the need to implement sustainable habits and initiatives at the local level, arguing in accordance with scientific knowledge of geology and environmental sciences about their positive effects and the urgency of adopting them. | 5.1 Promote and adopt sustainable habits based on the analysis of the uses of the different types of natural resources and the resulting environmental impacts.  5.2 Relate the impact of the exploitation of certain resources to environmental deterioration, arguing with a scientific basis the importance and need to adopt sustainable consumption habits. |

Currently, environmental degradation can be described as a global threat, which can lead to serious problems for the biosphere and for humanity itself as part of it. In order to slow the progress of these negative trends and avoid catastrophic consequences in the future, it is essential, first of all, to know the ecological, scientific, social and economic value of the natural world and to understand how our activities cause serious impacts. The development of this specific competence encourages students to observe the natural environment, directly or through information in different formats (photographs, satellite images, sections, hydrographic, geological, vegetation maps, among others) to analyze the use we make of natural resources in everyday objects and actions, and to promote reflection on the environmental impacts of the exploitation of resources, the problem of their scarcity and the importance of responsible management and consumption.

For these reasons, it is essential that students work on this competence, know the foundations that justify the urgent need to implement a sustainable development model and lead innovative initiatives and projects to promote and adopt sustainable habits in the individual and collective sphere.

**Competition 6**

**Identify and analyze geological elements of the relief using scientific knowledge with information in different formats or field observations, to explain phenomena, reconstruct geological history, make predictions and identify possible natural risks.**

**Evaluation criteria**

| 1st year | 2nd year |
| --- | --- |
| 6.1 Deduce and explain the geological history of a given area by identifying and analyzing its geological elements based on information in different formats (photographs, sections, geological maps, etc.).  6.2 Relate, using knowledge of geology and logical reasoning, the great events of Earth's history with elements of the geological record and with events that are currently taking place.  6.3 Solve dating problems by analyzing elements of the geological and fossil record and applying other methods. | 6.1 Deduce and explain the geological history of a given area by identifying and analyzing its geological elements based on information in different formats (photographs, sections, geological maps, etc.).  6.2 Make predictions about natural phenomena and risks in a given area by analyzing the influence of different factors (human activities, climatology, relief, vegetation, location, internal geological processes, etc.) and propose actions to prevent or minimize their negative effects. |

The study of the Earth based on the identification and analysis of the geological structures present in an area makes it possible to learn about the processes and phenomena that have occurred in the past, and thus be able to reconstruct its geological history, and make predictions about what may happen there in the future. Among the applications of this analytical process, we must mention the knowledge of the geological processes that occur on our planet, contextualized in the study area, but also, especially, the prediction and prevention of geological risks.

In the current context, in which the human species has a high occupation of the territory in practically all the continents, the interactions of our activities with the natural processes that occur there are numerous and complex, and very often generate risks for property and people's lives. Future projections regarding the frequency of these natural risks clearly indicate that they will increase due to climate change generated by human activities and the increase in population and human occupation of the territory. In the case of Mediterranean areas such as ours, these risks are particularly focused on the irregularity of rainfall. Therefore, the development of this specific competence for students involves the acquisition of knowledge and skills for the analysis of a territory through the observation of the natural environment or the study of various sources of geological and environmental information (such as photographs, sections or geological maps, among others), in order to become critical citizens with the ability to protect themselves, which will help with their actions to prevent or reduce natural risks and losses ecological, economic and human that these entail.

On the other hand, the application of methodologies based on direct and indirect dating tests and reasoning will allow students to understand the geological time scale and the relevance of the main geological and biological events that have occurred on our planet, contextualized in the study area.

Globally, the achievement of this competence will allow developing the appreciation for the geological heritage based on its knowledge and analysis and the assessment of the appropriate territorial planning, and rejecting abusive practices.

**know**

Knowledge, understood as the set of knowledge, skills, values ​​and attitudes, is formulated in relation to contexts in which competence learning can be developed. Teachers can incorporate alternative contexts if they consider it relevant. In order to facilitate learning and the development of the corresponding specific skills, teachers can assess the possibility of organizing the knowledge of the subject, or of the different subjects coordinated in an area, based on situations.

The situations make it possible to program the course of any level, subject or field from a collection or sequence of challenges, contexts and circumstances of the real world, from which derive questions that need to be answered and that intertwine knowledge, that is, knowledge, skills, values and attitudes, with the capacities that support the competence approach to learning, which modifies the usual planning of the acquisition of knowledge and competences based on academic logic specific to the areas of knowledge or subjects, embodied in the traditional sequence of disciplinary subjects. It aims to approach the learner's logic to give meaning to their learning based on the sequence of relevant contexts embodied in the situations.

**First year**

**Geology or environmental science scientific project**

- Assessment of the social relevance of the work of people dedicated to the study of geology and environmental sciences, recognizing the existing gender bias.
- Analysis of the historical evolution of scientific discoveries, understanding science as a collective, interdisciplinary and continuously building process.
- Assessment of the importance of the conservation of the geological and environmental heritage.

**Earth, a particular planet**

- Characterization of the Earth as a rocky planet.
- Analysis of the structure and characteristics of the atmosphere and hydrosphere and justification of their importance for living beings.
- Analysis of the internal geodynamics of the planet and its influence on the relief (volcanism, earthquakes, orogeny, continental movements, etc.) in view of the theory of plate tectonics.
- Relationship of the Wilson cycle with the changes in the arrangement of the continents and the main orogenic episodes.
- Relationship between the different types of rock deformations (elastic, plastic and brittle), with the forces and other factors acting on them.
- Analysis of external geological agents and processes (weathering, edaphogenesis, erosion, transport and sedimentation) and their effects on the relief.
- Relationship between the main forms of modeling the relief, the geological agents that originate them, the climate, the predominant rock types, the properties and the relative arrangement.
- Relationship between geological processes and human activities: concepts of natural and induced risk, resource, vulnerability, exposure, damage and preventive and corrective measures.

**Minerals, the components of rocks**

- Application of the mineral concept to differentiate minerals from other materials, based on cases from the environment.
- Classification of minerals on the basis of chemical composition and structure, and the relationship between these and their properties. Application to cases related to everyday life.
- Identification of minerals on the basis of their physical properties through the use of different tools (guides, keys, instruments, technological resources, etc.).
- Interpretation of phase diagrams of minerals to analyze the conditions of formation and transformation.
- Analysis of the importance of minerals and rocks and their everyday uses.

**Igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks**

- Application of the rock concept to differentiate rocks from minerals.
- Classification of rocks according to their origin (igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic) relating this to their observable characteristics.
- Identification using different tools (guides, keys, instruments, technological resources, etc.) of relevant rocks and the environment based on their characteristics.
- Interpretation of the composition and evolution of the different types of magmas, as well as the relationship with the resulting rocks, the characteristics of volcanic eruptions and the resulting reliefs.
- Analysis of the diagenesis process and its relationship with the formation of the different types of sedimentary rocks according to source material and sedimentary environment.
- Relationship between the types of metamorphic rocks and the factors that influence their formation.
- Analysis of the processes of formation, destruction and transformation of the different types of rocks in the lithological cycle and their relationship with plate tectonics and external geological processes.
- Discussion and exemplification of the importance of rocks in relation to their daily uses.

**History of the Earth and Life**

- Interpretation of the magnitude of geological time, the geological time scale and the application of dating methods.
- Solving geological dating problems using different methods.
- Analysis of the main geological and biological events throughout Earth's history and correlation with current processes and characteristics of our planet.

**Second year**

**Geological and environmental information**

- Search, recognition and use of truthful sources of geological and environmental information, in experimental research or observational studies formulated in the classroom.
- Interpretation of different sources of geological and environmental information (maps, sections, aerial photographs, texts, positioning and satellite images, flow diagrams, etc.) based on the environment.
- Representation of geological and environmental information using different tools (stratigraphic column, section, map, flow diagram, etc.).

**Plate tectonics and internal geodynamics**

- Interpretation of the key processes of the Earth's internal geodynamics (volcanism, earthquakes, orogeny, continental movements) and their influence on the relief in view of the theory of plate tectonics.
- Analysis of natural risks derived from internal geological processes and the relationship they have with human activities, valuing and justifying the importance of the appropriate planning of the territory and other preventive measures, based on examples from the environment.

**External geological processes**

- Interpretation of the agents and key processes of the external geodynamics of the Earth (weathering, edaphogenesis, erosion, transport and sedimentation) and their influence on the relief, based on relevant cases and the environment.
- Analysis of natural risks derived from external geological processes and the relationship they have with human activities, based on recent cases.
- Justification of the importance of preventive and corrective measures for the risks generated by external geological processes.

**The Fluid Layers of the Earth**

- Analysis of the dynamics of the atmosphere and hydrosphere and the natural risks caused by their interaction with human activities.
- Research and reflection on the causes and consequences of the main environmental impacts of human activities in the atmosphere (global warming, thinning of the ozone layer, acid rain, air pollution) and formulation of action proposals to minimize them, in the local and global environment.
- Relationship between certain human activities (deforestation, agriculture, intensive livestock farming, industrial activities, etc.) and the environmental impacts they generate in the hydrosphere, and formulation of action proposals to minimize them, in the local and global environment.
- Analysis of the relative abundance of water resources, exploitation, uses and assessment of the importance of water treatment methods for sustainable management.

**Natural resources and sustainable management**

- Reflection on the environment as an economic and social engine and on the importance of adopting a sustainable development model.
- Analysis of daily life activities using different sustainability indicators.
- Justification of the need to adopt lifestyles consistent with a sustainable development model.
- Analysis of the use of geological and energy resources in everyday life.
- Relationship between the different types of exploitation of rocks, minerals and energy resources of the geosphere and the environmental impacts they generate.
- Argumentation of the importance of responsible consumption of the different resources (water, landscape, mining, energy, soil, etc.) applying the concepts of resource, deposit, reserve, environmental impact, renewal rate and economic interest.
- Analysis of the characteristics, texture, structure, ecological relevance and productivity of the soil.
- Relationship between certain human activities (deforestation, intensive agriculture and livestock) and soil pollution and degradation.
- Justification of the importance of waste management in order to reduce it, value it, transform it and eliminate it.
- Analysis of preventive, corrective and compensatory measures for the environmental impacts caused by the exploitation of resources (water, landscape, mining, energy, soil, etc.).
- Participation in the main local and global initiatives aimed at implementing a sustainable development model.

<h2 class="accordion-header" id="headingQuimica">
<button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseQuimica" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="collapseQuimica">
