<div class="accordion-body">

[**Technology and Engineering**](https://xtec.gencat.cat/web/.content/curriculum/batxillerat/curriculum-171-2022/materias-de-modalitat/modalitat-ciencies-i-tecnologia/Tecnologia-i-Ingenyria.pdf){target="_blank"}

In today's society, the development of technology by engineering has become one of the axes around which socio-cultural evolution is articulated. In recent times, technology, understood as the set of knowledge derived from technique and engineering, with the contributions of scientific knowledge, and its instrumental and interdisciplinary nature, has played a fundamental role in the evolution of humanity, which will undoubtedly bring great changes and challenges in the society of the 21st century.

The main purpose of this subject is to continue developing and expanding the knowledge of the common subject of Technology and Digitization studied in compulsory secondary education, in which the minimum bases are established for scientific and technological literacy and for active and responsible participation in an increasingly changing society. In the fourth year of ESO, and with an optional nature, we find the Digitalization and Technology subjects, which correspond to an extension of the Technology and Digitalization subject.

It should be noted that technology and engineering have been increasing their relevance in different areas of society, from the generation of basic goods to communications. Despite this, inequalities still remain in today's society, with training, social, gender or generational gaps. It is also necessary to consider that the use of technology has generated negative impact situations that cannot be avoided, such as the massive use of thermal machines powered by fossil fuels, or programmed obsolescence, which is why it is necessary to consider that the ethical dimension and critical thinking must be part of the training in Technology and Engineering.

All of these aspects are related to the challenges that the 21st century poses to guarantee equal opportunities on a local and global scale. In an evolution towards a fairer and more balanced world, it is appropriate to pay attention to the mechanisms of technological society, analyzing and assessing the sustainability of production systems, the use of different materials and sources of energy, both in the industrial and domestic spheres and in services.

For this reason, citizens need to have a set of scientific and technological knowledge that serves as a basis to adopt critical and constructive attitudes towards certain issues and to be able to act in an ethical, responsible, creative, effective and environmentally sustainable manner, in order to provide solutions to the needs that arise.

In this sense, the subject of Technology and Engineering aims to unite scientific and technological knowledge with a competence approach to contribute to the achievement of the objectives of the high school stage and to the achievement of the students' key skills.

The specific competences of this subject are aimed at students developing technological projects that include analysis, research and design, in order to manufacture, automate and improve quality products and systems that respond to problems posed, while integrating knowledge from other areas of knowledge with an ethical and sustainable approach. The aim is to bring the students closer to the training and work environment typical of technological and engineering activity, advancing one more step in relation to the previous stage, especially in terms of technical knowledge. A committed and responsible attitude must be encouraged at all times, while promoting entrepreneurship, collaboration and local and global involvement with sustainable technological development. Thus, the resolution of interdisciplinary problems linked to real situations, through technological solutions, is constituted as a backbone of the subject's competence approach.

In this sense, students will be provided with a panoramic knowledge of the productive environment, taking into account reality and addressing everything that means the existence of a product, from its creation, its life cycle and other related aspects. This knowledge opens up a wide field of possibilities by facilitating the understanding of the design and development process from an industrial point of view and also through the application of active methodologies based on learning by doing and reflecting (*learning by doing*), of doing it yourself (*doing it yourself*), of customized or on-demand prototyping.

The coherence and continuity with previous stages is made explicit, especially in the subjects of Technology and Digitization, and Technology of compulsory secondary education, establishing between these a gradation in the level of complexity, in terms of the creation of technological solutions that respond to problems raised through the application of the technological process and other techniques.

This subject must help train students to effectively manage information in the processes of selection, reworking and construction of knowledge. The approach adopted must enable students to apply in an integrated manner the knowledge developed in the development of solutions to the problems raised. In the same way, the subject must make it possible, based on the learning developed and the ability to argue, with logical and ethical criteria, for students to adopt a suitably justified position and make coherent decisions when faced with a problem related to health and the environment.

Competences must be worked on from learning situations, in real or meaningful contexts, that invite students to reflect, collaborate and take action.

The achievement of the specific skills constitutes the basis for the student's competence assessment and will be assessed through the assessment criteria. There is no univocal and direct link between assessment criteria and knowledge. Specific skills will be assessed by putting different knowledge into action, in different situations, providing the necessary flexibility to establish connections with each other. In a competence approach, the evaluation criteria and knowledge are organized around specific competences.

Accompanying the specific skills of this subject are the assessment criteria, directly linked to the specific skills, which explain the assessment of the skills and knowledge that need to be developed, measure the degree of development of these skills and specify the learning we want to identify in the students and the way to do it. Their character is markedly competitive and makes them evaluators not only of theoretical content, but also of the skills and attitudes that students must acquire in order to develop in a society that demands a critical spirit both in the face of scientific questions and others of a social nature, in which science plays an important role. The teaching staff must contextualize and make these criteria more flexible in accordance with the circumstances of their activity.

The subject is organized around the blocks of basic knowledge in both the first year and the second, the contents of which must be interrelated through the development of activities or projects of a practical nature, which are contextualized and close to the students for integration, management and subsequent resolution.

The first block, *research and development projects*, focuses on the project methodology, aimed at the ideation and creation of products, as well as their life cycle. The second block, *materials and manufacturing*, addresses the criteria for selecting materials and the most appropriate techniques for their transformation and the development of sustainable technological solutions. The third block, *mechanical systems*, refers to elements, mechanisms and systems that can serve as a basis for the development of projects or for the ideation of technical solutions. In the fourth block, *electrical and electronic systems*, the main characteristics and existing differences between direct current and alternating current, the design, simulation and/or construction of circuits that allow analysis, experimentation and interpretation of their operation are studied. The fifth block, *automation*, addresses the updating of technological systems for automatic control, taking into account the potential offered by emerging technologies based especially on digitization and communications. Finally, the sixth block, *sustainable technology*, provides students with a vision of the subject aligned with the need to consider the limitation of available resources and the social and environmental impact of technology, consistent with some milestones of the sustainable development objectives.

In this sense, with the aim of conferring a competence approach to the subject, it is convenient that knowledge can come together in projects that involve a contextualized learning situation, in which students can apply their knowledge and skills to provide a solution to a specific need, which can emerge from a personal, social or cultural context, at the local or global level, with an attitude of increasing commitment, so that the creation of links between the educational environment and other social, economic or research sectors.

This professional and practical approach makes it necessary to use a technology workshop classroom that evolves into a manufacturing laboratory, with the necessary equipment to develop projects that integrate digital manufacturing. It must allow the incorporation of work techniques, rapid prototyping and offline manufacturing (*offline)*, with great potential for development, in accordance with the demands of our society and our production system.

**Specific skills**

**Competition 1**

**Analyze, coordinate and design research projects with a critical and entrepreneurial attitude, devising and implementing sustainable and efficient problem-solving strategies and techniques, while communicating the results in an orderly and reasoned manner, to create and continuously improve products and systems.**

**Evaluation criteria**

| 1st year | 2nd year |
| --- | --- |
| 1.1 Research and design technical projects that show the creation and improvement of a product or system, arguing it through the interpretation and referencing of information.  1.2 Participate in the development and coordination of projects for the continuous creation and innovation of viable and socially responsible products, identifying improvements and creating prototypes through an iterative process, with an entrepreneurial attitude.  1.3 Collaborate in technological tasks, showing a proactive attitude and respect towards the contributions and reasoning carried out by all members of the group, promoting cooperation and group well-being.  1.4 Prepare the technical documentation, in a precise and accurate manner, that includes the most significant textual, numerical and graphic information while using digital applications.  1.5 Communicate technological ideas and solutions in an effective and organized manner, using appropriate support, terminology and rigor. | 1.1 Develop research and innovation projects with the aim of creating and improving products in a continuous and sustainable manner, using cooperative and flexible management models.  1.2 Communicate, argue and disseminate the elaborated project in a clear, orderly and comprehensible manner, presenting the technical documentation while using digital applications.  1.3 Persevere in achieving goals in situations of uncertainty, identifying and managing emotions, accepting and learning from reasoned criticism and using error as part of the learning process. |

This specific competence involves the participation of students in the resolution of technical problems, as well as the coordination and management of cooperative and collaborative research projects. This involves, among other aspects, showing empathy, establishing and maintaining positive relationships, exercising active listening and assertive communication, identifying and managing emotions in the learning process, recognizing sources of stress and being persevering in achieving goals. Additionally, specific research techniques are incorporated, facilitating the ideation and decision-making process, and iterative strategies to organize and plan the tasks to be developed by the teams, solving from a basic initial solution that, in several phases, will be completed at a functional level while establishing different priorities. In this aspect, the method of designer thinking (*design thinking*) and agile methodologies (Agile) are commonly used in technology companies, as they provide greater flexibility in the face of any change in customer demands. The continuous improvement of products is also taken into account as a starting point for projects to be developed, which is a reflection of what is happening in the industrial field. Overcoming stereotypes and preconceived ideas associated with technological subjects and engineering, such as gender, must be encouraged. In this specific competence, research should be emphasized as an approach to R+D+I projects, in a critical and creative way, where the correct referencing of information and the preparation of technical documentation acquire great importance. Therefore, the development of this competence entails expressing complex facts, ideas, concepts and procedures in a unified, analytical and graphical manner, truthfully and precisely, using the appropriate terminology, to communicate and disseminate the ideas and solutions generated.

**Competition 2**

**Compare and select materials, applying technical and sustainable criteria, to manufacture quality products and prepare impact studies that provide answers to problems or situations raised with an ethical and eco-socially responsible approach.**

**Evaluation criteria**

| 1st year | 2nd year |
| --- | --- |
| 2.1 Determine the life cycle of a product, planning and applying quality control measures at the different stages, from design to marketing, taking into account continuous improvement strategies.  2.2 Compare and select materials, traditional or new generation, for the manufacture of quality products based on technical characteristics and meeting sustainability criteria in a responsible and ethical manner.  2.3 Make models or prototypes using the most appropriate manufacturing techniques, applying technical and sustainable criteria. | 2.1 Analyze and assess the suitability of technical materials in the manufacture of sustainable and quality products, while studying the internal structure, properties and treatments to modify and improve their properties.  2.2 Prepare, argue and disseminate technical environmental impact assessment reports that assess the repercussions that may arise from the implementation of a technical project. |

This competence refers to the ability to compare and select the most suitable materials for the creation of products based on their characteristics, as well as carry out the study and evaluation of the environmental impact generated. When determining the materials, criteria relating to the technical properties will be met (aspects such as hardness, resistance, electrical conductivity, thermal insulation, etc.). Similarly, students will take into account aspects related to the ability to be conformed by applying one technique or another, as appropriate for the final application of the product. In addition, the criteria relating to the material's ability to be treated, modified or alloyed in order to improve its final characteristics must be considered. Finally, students will assess aspects of sustainability to determine which materials are the most appropriate in relation to the pollution generated and energy consumption throughout the life cycle. Equally, it is necessary to consider the ability to recycle at the end of its useful life, the biodegradability of the material and other aspects linked to the controlled use of resources or to the relationship established between the materials and the people who ultimately use the product.

**Competition 3**

**Select, use and configure the necessary digital tools, applying interdisciplinary knowledge, to solve tasks and communicate the results in an orderly and precise manner, with careful use of graphic language and appropriate technical terminology.**

**Evaluation criteria**

| 1st year | 2nd year |
| --- | --- |
| 3.1 Solve independently and optimally proposed tasks and functions, through the use and configuration of different digital tools, while applying interdisciplinary knowledge.  3.2 Carry out the presentation of technical projects, arguing the decisions taken, while using the most suitable digital applications for each situation. | 3.1 Solve the problems associated with the different phases of the development and management of a technical project (design, simulation, assembly and presentation), using the appropriate tools and digital applications. |

At this stage, the competition addresses the aspects related to the incorporation of digitization in the usual learning process. Therefore, and continuing with the skills acquired in the previous stage, the use of digital tools is expanded and strengthened in the tasks associated with the subject. Examples are activities linked to research, the search and selection of information or the analysis of technological products and systems, making good use of information search tools, assessing its provenance and contrasting its reliability while making a critical analysis. Collaborative work, the communication of ideas or the dissemination and presentation of work consolidate new learning and involve knowledge of the characteristics of available communication tools, their applications, options and functionalities, depending on the context. In the same way, the design and creation process is complemented by a set of programs that allow the dimensioning, simulation, programming and control of systems or the manufacture of products. The use and application of digital tools, to facilitate the creation of solutions and the improvement of results, become essential instruments in any of the phases of the process. They cover activities related to the management, design or development of technological solutions, as well as those related to the practical resolution of simple exercises or the preparation and dissemination of technical documentation related to projects.

**Competition 4**

**Build new knowledge and improve technical skills, applying and transferring knowledge from other disciplines with a creative attitude, to calculate, measure and solve problems or provide answers to different needs specific to the fields of engineering.**

**Evaluation criteria**

| 1st year | 2nd year |
| --- | --- |
| 4.1 Experiment, measure, interpret and solve problems associated with mechanical installation systems by applying the fundamentals of movement transmission and transformation mechanisms.  4.2 Experiment, measure, interpret and solve problems associated with fixed and mobile mechanical support and joining systems.  4.3 Experiment, measure, interpret and solve problems associated with systems of electronic circuits and electrical installations, while applying the fundamentals of direct current circuits, as well as rotating electrical machines. | 4.1 Calculate, simulate and experiment with simple structures, analyzing and evaluating the types of loads to which they may be subjected, while evaluating their efforts and stability.  4.2 Analyze and compare the different thermal machines: refrigerating machines, heat pumps and thermal engines, differentiating and interpreting their operation and carrying out the essential calculations to be able to determine their efficiency.  4.3 Interpret, design, simulate or build pneumatic automation circuits, relating each of the elements of the circuit to the operation of the system.  4.4 Interpret, design and simulate oleo-hydraulic circuits, relating each of the elements of the circuit to the operation of the system.  4.5 Experiment and design physical and simulated combinational and sequential circuits applying fundamentals of digital electronics and explaining their operation in the design of technological solutions. |

The resolution of a simple exercise or a complex technological problem requires the application of techniques, procedures and knowledge offered by different areas of scientific knowledge. This specific competence has, on the one hand, the purpose of students using the knowledge acquired in the subjects of mathematics or fundamentals of physics or chemistry, to calculate magnitudes and variables of mechanical, electrical, electronic, automation problems or to develop programs. On the other hand, it can use experimentation, through assemblies or simulations, as a tool for consolidating the knowledge acquired. This transfer of knowledge applied to new and diverse problems or situations, allows students to expand their knowledge and foster the ability to learn to learn.

**Competition 5**

**Design, create and evaluate technological systems applying knowledge of automatic regulation, programmed control and the possibilities offered by emerging technologies, to study, control and automate tasks in technological and robotic systems.**

**Evaluation criteria**

| 1st year | 2nd year |
| --- | --- |
| 5.1 Control and experience the operation of technological and robotic systems, using programming languages ​​and applying the possibilities offered by emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, telemetry, the Internet of Things, massive data processing (*big* *data*), etc.  5.2 Automate, program and experience robot functionalities and trajectories, by modeling them and applying simple algorithms. | 5.1 Interpret, simulate and experience the operation of technological processes based on automatic open-loop and closed-loop systems, applying simplification techniques and analyzing their stability. |

This specific competence refers to the suitability of products or technological solutions so that they can perform certain tasks autonomously. It is about incorporating elements of automatic regulation or programmed control in the designs, allowing simple actions in machines or technological systems. In this sense, they include, for example, the control of displacements or movements of the elements of a robot, the regulated actuation of actuators, such as lights or motors, the stability of the values ​​of specific quantities, etc. In this way, it is possible for students to automate tasks on machines and robots by implementing appropriate programs on control cards. In this line of action, the role of emerging technologies (artificial intelligence, internet of things, *big data*, etc.) applied to the control of objects should be highlighted.

**Competition 6**

**Identify and analyze the different technological systems in the fields of engineering, studying and comparing their characteristics, all the while valuing the use of energy and energy efficiency to evaluate and value the sustainable and eco-socially responsible use of technology.**

**Evaluation criteria**

| 1st year | 2nd year |
| --- | --- |
| 6.1 Analyze and evaluate the different electrical energy generation and distribution systems and the characteristics of the energy markets, developing the necessary calculations to determine and assess their efficiency and environmental, social and economic impact. | 6.1 Analyze the different installations of a home from the point of view of energy efficiency, looking for those options most committed to sustainability and applying solutions based on low energy requirements and renewable energies. |

The objective pursued by this specific competence is to provide students with an informed judgment about the use and impact of energy in society and the environment, through the acquisition of an overview of the different energy systems, the agents involved and the basic aspects related to domestic supplies. In a complementary way, it is intended to provide students with the criteria to be used in the evaluation of the social and environmental impact linked to projects of a diverse nature. For the development of this competence, on the one hand, the systems of generation, transport, distribution of energy and supply are addressed, as well as the functioning of energy markets. On the other hand, work is being done on the installations in homes of thermal machines and automatic regulation foundations, taking into account criteria related to efficiency and energy saving, encouraging students to make responsible and sustainable use of technology.

**know**

Knowledge, understood as the set of knowledge, skills, values ​​and attitudes, is formulated in relation to contexts in which competence learning can be developed. Teachers can incorporate alternative contexts if they consider it relevant. In order to facilitate learning and the development of the corresponding specific skills, teachers can assess the possibility of organizing the knowledge of the subject, or of the different subjects coordinated in an area, based on situations.

The situations make it possible to program the course of any level, subject or field from a collection or sequence of challenges, contexts and circumstances of the real world, from which derive questions that need to be answered and that intertwine knowledge, that is, knowledge, skills, values and attitudes, with the capacities that support the competence approach to learning, which modifies the usual planning of the acquisition of knowledge and competences based on academic logic specific to the areas of knowledge or subjects, embodied in the traditional sequence of disciplinary subjects. It aims to approach the learner's logic to give meaning to their learning based on the sequence of relevant contexts embodied in the situations.

**First year**

**Research and development projects**

- Project management and development strategies: designer thinking (*design thinking*). Research and ideation techniques.
- Application of project management and development strategies based on designer thinking and research and ideation techniques, in the personal, social or cultural context, on a local or global level.
- Products of the immediate environment: life cycle. Continuous improvement strategies. Planning and development of design and marketing. Logistics, transport and distribution. Metrology and standardization. Quality control.
- Analysis of the life cycle of different products, applying continuous improvement strategies. Planning and development of the design and marketing of different products with the optimization of logistics, transport and distribution.
- Planning of quality control techniques in production. Application of metrology and industrial standardization.
- Graphic expression. CAD-CAE-CAM applications. Functional diagrams, diagrams and sketches.
- Use of different graphic expression tools and applications for computer-aided design, analysis and manufacturing (CAD-CAE-CAM). Elaboration of functional diagrams and schemes with digital tools and sketches in real situations.
- Entrepreneurship, resilience, perseverance and creativity to address problems from an interdisciplinary perspective, based on relevant examples.
- Solving tasks and projects with an entrepreneurial, resilient, persevering and creative attitude to approach problems from an interdisciplinary perspective.
- Self-confidence and initiative. Identification and management of emotions. Error and reassessment as part of the learning process in different contexts; personal, social or cultural, at the local or global level.
- Development of self-confidence and personal initiative. Identification and management of emotions, valuing error and re-evaluation as part of the learning process.

**Materials and manufacturing**

- Technical materials and new materials. classification Selection and characteristic applications based on contextualized and real examples.
- Analysis and comparison of the characteristics of different technical materials and newly created materials. Differentiation and selection of materials according to their uses and applications. Application to cases raised in the classroom.
- Manufacturing techniques: rapid and on-demand prototyping. Digital manufacturing applied to projects.
- Description of the main industrial manufacturing techniques for obtaining technological products made with various materials such as metals, plastic and wood. Specific machinery. Possible applications to real situations.
- Design and rapid creation of prototypes with the use of digital manufacturing contextualized in the school environment.
- Application of digital manufacturing, on demand, for the customized production of projects with efficient, innovative and environmentally friendly solutions, based on real cases.
- Safety and hygiene rules at work in the work and school environment.
- Application of safety and hygiene rules in the development of tasks in the different work spaces.

**Mechanical Systems**

- Movement transmission and transformation mechanisms. Supports and joining of mechanical elements. Design, calculation, assembly and physical or simulated experimentation. Practical application to projects proposed in the classroom.
- Description of the different mechanisms of movement transmission and transformation and specification of their characteristics and geometric parameters, based on nearby examples.
- Design, calculation, assembly and physical or simulated experimentation of mechanical systems that have a practical application in the projects to be developed.

**Electrical and electronic systems**

- Direct current circuits and electrical machines. Interpretation and schematic representation of circuits, calculation, assembly and physical or simulated experimentation. Application to projects.
- Interpretation and representation of direct current electrical circuit diagrams and analog electronic circuits using standardized symbology. Project documentation.
- Design, calculation, simulation, assembly, measurement and experimentation of direct current electrical circuits and basic analog electronic circuits, in the school context.
- Description, calculation and application of rotary direct current machines integrated in projects.

**Automation**

- Text programming languages. Creation of programs applied to process automation based on real examples.
- Creation of programs applied to the automation of processes with textual and graphic programming languages.
- Control systems. Concepts and elements. Modeling of simple systems and study of possible applications in the real world.
- Analysis of control systems. Definition of concepts and elements of a system. Modeling of simple systems.
- Artificial intelligence applied to control systems based on examples from the immediate environment.
- Analysis of artificial intelligence programs applied to control systems.
- Communication protocols. Telemetry and monitoring. Internet of things and massive data processing (*big data*), based on relevant examples.
- Description of communication protocols in automation systems. Uses of telemetry and monitoring. Description of the applications of the internet of things and massive data processing (*big data*).
- Robotics: modeling of movements and mechanical actions applied to contexts close to the student.
- Application of robotics. Design, modeling and programming of movement trajectories and mechanical actions.

**Sustainable technology**

- Energy systems and markets. Sustainable energy consumption, saving techniques and criteria. Domestic supplies.
- Analysis of energy systems and markets. Description of primary energy sources and their origin. Analysis of the impact of energy costs on the economy and society. Characterization of the energy transition to renewable energies based on examples from the immediate environment.
- Sustainable use of energy, techniques and criteria for responsible use in different fields of engineering.
- Description of the different types of household supplies and specific regulations. Application to cases of the environment close to the students.
- Installations in homes: electrical, water and air conditioning, communication and home automation. Renewable energies, energy efficiency and sustainability.
- Characterization of the installations in homes: electrical, water and air conditioning, communication and home automation. Description of bioclimatism: renewable energies, energy efficiency and sustainability. Analysis of emerging energy technologies: aerothermia, photovoltaic self-consumption and geothermal energy. Application to cases of the environment close to the students.

**Second year**

**Research and development projects**

- Management and development of projects with the application of different techniques and teamwork strategies. Agile methodologies. Types, characteristics and applications based on examples from the immediate environment.
- Dissemination and communication of technical documentation. Preparation, referencing and presentation in the school context.
- Self-confidence and initiative. Identification and management of emotions. Error and reassessment as part of the learning process in cases close to the students.
- Development of self-confidence and initiative. Identification and management of emotions, valuing error and re-evaluation as part of the learning process.
- Entrepreneurship, resilience, perseverance and creativity to approach problems from an interdisciplinary perspective based on real cases.
- Solving tasks and projects with an entrepreneurial, resilient, persevering and creative attitude to approach problems from an interdisciplinary perspective.

**Materials and manufacturing**

- Internal structure Properties and test procedures based on examples of different materials.
- Analysis of the internal structure of materials. Determination of the properties and testing procedures of materials.
- Design techniques and treatments for modification and improvement of properties and sustainability. Industrial manufacturing techniques based on recent and relevant examples.
- Description of design techniques and treatments for modification and improvement of material properties and sustainability. Industrial manufacturing techniques based on relevant cases.

**Mechanical Systems**

- Simple structures. Types of loads, stability and basic calculations based on nearby examples.
- Analysis of simple structures. Identification of the types of loads, determination of stability and carrying out basic calculations. Simulation and experimentation of simple examples.
- Thermal machines: refrigerating machine, heat pump and thermal engines. Basic calculations and applications in the immediate environment.
- Characterization of thermal machines: refrigerating machine, heat pump and thermal engines. Performing basic calculations, simulations and applications.
- Pneumatics and hydraulics: components and physical principles. Description and analysis. Characteristic schemes of application. Physical or simulated design and assembly based on real cases.
- Description and analysis of pneumatic and electropneumatic automatisms: components and physical principles. Interpretation and representation of characteristic application schemes. Design, simulation and assembly of pneumatic and electropneumatic circuits.
- Description and analysis of hydraulic circuits: components and physical principles. Interpretation and representation of characteristic application schemes.

**Electrical and electronic systems**

- Alternating current circuits. Triangle of powers. Calculation, assembly or simulation.
- Analysis, calculation and assembly or simulation of alternating current circuits. Calculation of powers and determination of the triangle of powers.
- Combinational digital electronics. Design and simplification. Experimentation in simulators.
- Design, representation and application of combinational digital electronics circuits. Application of Boolean algebra and simplification of expressions and circuits. Simulation and experimentation of circuits, based on real cases.
- Sequential digital electronics. Experimentation in simulators.
- Design, representation and application of sequential digital electronic circuits. Simulation and experimentation of circuits.

**Automation**

- Algebra of blocks and simplification of systems. stability Experimentation in simulators.
- Analysis of control systems and their applications. Identification and representation of control blocks. Determination of the parameters of a control system and its stability. Experimentation or simulation.

**Sustainable technology**

- Social and environmental impact. Evaluation reports. Critical assessment of sustainability in the use of technology, based on real cases.
- Determination of the social and environmental impacts of a technological project. Elaboration of impact assessment reports. Critical assessment of sustainability in the use of technology.

<h2 class="accordion-header" id="headingRob">
<button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseRob" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="collapseRob">
<strong>🤖 Ciències Generals - Matèries obligatòries de modalitat</strong>
</button>
</h2>
<div id="collapseRob" class="accordion-collapse collapse" aria-labelledby="headingRob" data-bs-parent="#competenciasAccordion">
<div class="accordion-body">

[**General Sciences**](https://xtec.gencat.cat/web/.content/curriculum/batxillerat/curriculum-171-2022/materias-obligatories-de-modalitat/Ciencies-Generals.pdf){target="_blank"}

In today's society there are many aspects that are related to scientific activity, both in the health field and in the environmental, technological or economic fields. For this reason, the fact of having a solid scientific training allows people to form and defend a well-founded opinion in the face of controversial facts that are part of the day-to-day life of our world. This subject offers students basic training in the four fundamental scientific disciplines. In addition, its multidisciplinary approach gives the curriculum a unifying character that highlights that the different sciences are a specialization of a global and coherent whole that is scientific knowledge. In fact, in the development of research as a professional activity, scientists relate knowledge, skills and attitudes from all disciplines to enrich their studies and contribute more efficiently to the progress of society.

This subject can be accessed by different profiles of students, with different previous training in science, which is why the acquisition of learning in this subject is built on those that all students have developed during compulsory secondary education, and from there it is deepened to achieve the skills and objectives specific to the high school stage.

The subject of General Sciences aims to provide students who take it with a sufficient basis to understand the general principles that govern the phenomena of the natural world. For this, this subject starts from the specific competencies, which aim to understand, explain and know how to mobilize knowledge, skills and attitudes not only related to the situation and repercussions of science at the present time, but also to the procedures of scientific activity and their relevance in social developments, the need for equal treatment between people and the consistent and global nature of the set of scientific disciplines.

This subject must help train students to effectively manage information in the processes of selection, reworking and construction of knowledge. The approach adopted must enable students to apply the knowledge developed in an integrated way, either in the production of texts that respond to a specific format and situation or in the design of experimental research applied to the verification of a hypothesis or the development of solutions to problems applied in various contexts. In the same way, the subject must make it possible for students, based on the learning developed and the ability to argue, with logical and ethical criteria, to adopt a suitably justified position and make coherent decisions when faced with a social, political, economic, environmental, health, scientific, etc. problem.

Competences must be worked on from learning situations, in real or meaningful contexts, that invite students to reflect, collaborate and take action.

The achievement of the specific skills constitutes the basis for the student's competence assessment and will be assessed through the assessment criteria. There is no univocal and direct link between assessment criteria and knowledge. Specific skills will be assessed by putting different knowledge into action, in different situations, and the necessary flexibility will be provided to establish connections between them. In a competence approach, the evaluation criteria and knowledge are organized around specific competences.

Accompanying the specific skills of this subject are the evaluation criteria. They are directly linked to the specific skills, they explain the assessment of the skills and knowledge that needs to be developed, they measure the degree of development of these skills and specify the learning we want to identify in the students and the way to do it. Their character is markedly competitive and makes them evaluators not only of theoretical content, but also of the skills and attitudes that students must acquire in order to develop in a society that demands a critical spirit both in the face of scientific issues and others of a social nature where science plays an important role. The teaching staff must contextualize and make these criteria more flexible in accordance with the circumstances of their activity.

The development of specific skills is based on the key skills and knowledge of the subject, which are structured in five blocks that include essential knowledge, skills and attitudes. For this reason, it is chosen to formulate the knowledge linked to a capacity and in a context in which they must be developed. The teaching staff can develop an alternative context, if they consider it appropriate.

The first block of knowledge deals with the basic aspects of general scientific activity: the use of scientific methodologies for the study of natural phenomena, experimentation - including the necessary instruments and their rules of use -, the appropriate use of scientific languages ​​and relevant mathematical tools, etc. This blog seeks to develop practical skills useful for the rest of the blogs.

Block 2 describes two fundamental concepts of science: matter and energy. Knowing and using these concepts with agility is basic for all areas of study and work in science, as it is the basis on which knowledge of physicochemical, biological and geological systems must be built.

Block 3 works with the fundamental forces of nature and the effects they have on systems. These are transversal contents for all the disciplines of science, which make it possible to give explanations to aspects as important as movement, the deformations of the earth's crust or the movement of the planets of the solar system.

Block 4 provides an approach to the study of the Earth and terrestrial systems from the point of view of planetary geology, plate tectonics and the dynamics of fluid layers. In addition, emphasis is placed on key aspects aimed at raising students' awareness of sustainable development and health promotion.

Block 5 deals with some questions about biotechnology and its importance in researching diseases, agricultural and livestock techniques or environmental recovery, etc.

In short, the General Sciences curriculum aims to provide students with the basic tools to recognize the importance of the sciences, the creation of scientific vocations and the development of their own and well-founded criteria for the application of scientific ideas over pseudo-scientific and misleading statements. Given that it is characteristic of work in scientific research, the tools provided by this curriculum invite the development of projects and interdisciplinary cooperation between different individuals or entities, with special attention to the problems inherent in the objectives of sustainable development. This gives the learning of science a relevant, holistic and integrated character, which enriches the significance and prepares students to face their active incorporation as adults in society.

**Specific skills**

**Competition 1**

**Apply the various forms of reasoning typical of science and carry out experimental research and observational studies using accurate material and appropriate instruments to answer questions that occur in the environment about physical, chemical, biological and geological processes**

**Evaluation criteria**

1.1 Define researchable problems, formulate hypotheses and coherently plan research processes in accordance with the forms of reasoning typical of scientific thinking

1.2 Develop research processes to verify or discard the hypotheses formulated regarding a researchable problem or scientific phenomenon applying all the measures typical of experimental work.

1.3 Process the information derived from research through the construction of tables, graphs, models, simulations, diagrams or other formats and interpret the natural phenomena expressed by these instruments.

1.4 Communicate the results of a research through the use of appropriate resources and in accordance with basic ethical principles.

1.5 Elaborate the conclusions of a research highlighting the relationship between the results and the theoretical framework in which they are interpreted.

To achieve basic scientific literacy, each student must first of all understand what the *modus operandi* of the entire scientific community is when it comes to the study of natural phenomena and what tools are available. Scientific methodologies are fundamental working procedures in science. Competent students must develop the skills to observe, hypothesize and experiment on physicochemical and natural phenomena, as well as those that allow them to share the results they obtain with the rest of the research community.

Also, even if the student does not choose in the future to dedicate himself to science as a professional activity, the development of this competence gives him some abilities and skills specific to scientific thinking.

**Competition 2**

**Apply current principles, laws and scientific theories in the explanation and prediction of the behavior of the phenomena and components of the environment to acquire a holistic view of the functioning of nature**

**Evaluation criteria**

2.1 Apply current scientific knowledge in the elaboration of explanations and predictions of the behavior of the phenomena that occur in nature.

2.2 Recognize, analyze and interpret the most relevant physicochemical phenomena using the main physical and chemical laws.

2.3 Recognize, analyze and interpret the basic elements and processes of the biosphere and geosphere using current scientific foundations.

The development of scientific competence has as an essential basis understanding the observed phenomena of nature referring to processes, natural elements of the environment, technological artifacts, etc., and interpreting them in view of principles, laws and basic scientific theories. The development of this specific competence also contributes to the acquisition of scientific thinking, key to the creation of new knowledge based on the principles, laws and theories of science.

In addition, the mobilization of practical knowledge, that is, the ability to find a direct application to the theoretical knowledge learned, is in line with the principles of STEM learning, which aims to create a global learning of the sciences as an integrated whole of interrelated disciplines. Students who study this subject learn to relate concepts, because they find a clear example of the knowledge, skills and attitudes that are the basis for a general scientific literacy and that are presented together, given that science is a set of knowledge dependent on each other.

**Competition 3**

**Argue about the importance of incorporating healthy and sustainable habits based on scientific foundations to adopt and promote them in your environment.**

**Evaluation criteria**

3.1 Review and evaluate your own ideas in relation to the adoption of a lifestyle compatible with a sustainable development model.

3.2 Defend and justify, making coherent proposals for action and using scientific foundations from different disciplines, the importance of personal commitment and the adoption of a lifestyle compatible with a model of sustainable development.

3.3 Review and evaluate your own ideas in relation to the adoption of a healthy lifestyle (balanced diet, rejection of drug use, physical exercise, sleep hygiene, appropriate postures, etc.).

3.4 Defend and justify, making coherent proposals for action and using foundations derived from human physiology, the importance of adopting and promoting healthy habits.

Currently, one of the biggest and most important challenges facing humanity is environmental degradation that endangers economic development and welfare society. An indispensable condition for addressing this challenge is to adopt a sustainable development model. For this reason, it is essential that citizens understand their dependence on the natural environment in order to value the importance of its conservation and to act consistently and committed to this objective.

The achievement and development of this specific competence will allow students, through knowledge of the functioning of their own body and ecosystems, to understand the relationship between health, environmental conservation and economic development and thus become a committed and critical citizen with the problems of our time.

**Competition 4**

**Apply the knowledge and the various forms of reasoning specific to science, keeping an open mind in relation to the procedures you follow and the results you obtain to solve problems related to the experimental sciences**

**Evaluation criteria**

4.1 Apply knowledge and the various forms of reasoning specific to science in solving problems related to physical, chemical, biological and geological phenomena and processes, looking for alternative resolution strategies when necessary.

4.2 Maintain an open mind based on the critical analysis of proposed solutions for problems related to physical, chemical, biological and geological phenomena and processes, reformulating, if necessary, the strategies followed or the conclusions drawn if the available data suggest so.

Reasoning is an essential tool in scientific research, given that it is necessary in the formulation of hypotheses or new strategies that allow us to continue progressing in the face of difficulties to achieve the proposed objectives. Likewise, in certain scientific disciplines it is not possible to obtain direct evidence of the processes or objects of study, so it is necessary to use logical reasoning to be able to connect the results with the reality they reflect. Similarly, it is common to find scenarios in everyday life that require the use of logic and reasoning.

It should also be noted that problem solving is a complex process in which not only reasoning skills are mobilized, but also subject matter knowledge and attitudes to face challenges in a positive way. For this reason, it is essential that students develop this specific competence, as it will allow them to mature intellectually and improve their resilience in order to successfully address different types of situations that they will face throughout their professional, social and personal lives.

**Competition 5**

**Justify the contribution of science, conceived as a collective and interdisciplinary process and under continuous construction, to society and highlight the function of the people who dedicate themselves to it, to evaluate its essential role in the progress of humanity.**

**Evaluation criteria**

5.1 Provide arguments that demonstrate that science is an area of ​​global knowledge made up of different disciplines that are related to each other and dependent on each other.

5.2 Demonstrate the relevance of science for the progress of society, as well as the important role that men and women play in carrying out scientific research as a work activity.

Currently, a significant number of people dedicate their work to scientific research and technological development. However, and even if the situation is improving little by little, science does not always enjoy the recognition and repercussion it deserves and, sometimes, the value of the contribution of science to improvement and progress is not sufficiently valued, generally due to the lack of substantiated information and the dissemination of erroneous information. Fighting to improve this situation and form citizens with a rich scientific culture and so that more and more men and women have a vocation to dedicate themselves to scientific activities, is fundamental to achieving the development of a better world.

Through this specific competence, students become aware of the relevance of science in today's society. Likewise, it recognizes the interdisciplinary nature of science, marked by a clear interdependence between the different disciplines of knowledge that enriches all scientific activity and that is reflected in a holistic development of research and work in science.

**Competition 6**

**Use varied resources, of various types and formats, to search for and select reliable and verified information and establish collaborations applying critical and ethical sense.**

**Evaluation criteria**

6.1 Search, contrast, select and combine information on physical, chemical, biological or geological phenomena and processes in different formats and using the necessary resources, technological or otherwise.

6.2 Establish collaborations using the necessary resources, technological or not, in the different stages of the scientific project, in carrying out activities or solving problems related to physical, chemical, biological or geological phenomena and processes.

Communication and collaboration are inherent components of the process of scientific progress. Part of this communicative process involves searching for and selecting scientific information published by reliable sources, which must be interpreted to answer specific questions and establish well-founded conclusions. For this reason, it is necessary to analyze the information obtained critically, taking into account its origin and differentiating the appropriate sources from those less reliable.

Cooperation is another essential aspect of scientific methodologies and aims to improve the efficiency of work by joining the efforts of several people through the exchange of information, thus achieving a synergistic effect.

In addition, developing this specific competence is very useful in other non-scientific professional environments, as well as in the social and personal context, such as lifelong learning or the exercise of active democratic citizenship. Communication and collaboration involve the deployment of social skills, a critical sense, respect for diversity and, often, efficient, ethical and responsible use of technological resources, so this competence is essential for the full development of students as citizens.

 **know**

Knowledge, understood as the set of knowledge, skills, values ​​and attitudes, is formulated in relation to contexts in which competence learning can be developed. Teachers can incorporate alternative contexts if they consider it relevant. In order to facilitate learning and the development of the corresponding specific skills, teachers can assess the possibility of organizing the knowledge of the subject, or of the different subjects coordinated in an area, based on situations.

The situations make it possible to program the course of any level, subject or field from a collection or sequence of challenges, contexts and circumstances of the real world, from which derive questions that need to be answered and that intertwine knowledge, that is, knowledge, skills, values and attitudes, with the capacities that support the competence approach to learning, which modifies the usual planning of the acquisition of knowledge and competences based on academic logic specific to the areas of knowledge or subjects, embodied in the traditional sequence of disciplinary subjects. It aims to approach the learner's logic to give meaning to their learning based on the sequence of relevant contexts embodied in the situations.

**Building Science**

- Use of scientific research methodologies for the identification and formulation of questions and conjectures, the development of hypotheses and their experimental verification in the resolution of researchable problems.
- Design and execution of experiments and experimental research projects and observational studies using appropriate instruments, experimental controls and logical reasoning and analysis of the results obtained in the resolution of scientific problems and issues related to the environment.
- Recognition and use of reliable sources and means of collaboration for the search of scientific information in different formats and the use of the necessary tools.
- Interpretation and production of scientific information with appropriate language to develop a criterion based on evidence and reasoning.
- Evaluation of the contribution of scientists to the main milestones of science for the progress and improvement of society.

**A universe of matter and energy**

- Analysis of the macroscopic properties of material systems and states of aggregation, as well as the physical and chemical processes of change using microscopic models.
- Classification of material systems according to their composition, applying them to the description of natural systems and the resolution of related problems.
- Recognition of the historical and current importance of the periodic table, describing the regularities observed in it and the relationship with the internal structure of matter.
- Study of the formation of chemical compounds, interpretation of their formulation and nomenclature as a basis for a basic scientific literacy that allows to establish efficient communication with the entire scientific community.
- Application of the chemical transformations of material systems and the laws that govern them, in the industrial, environmental and social processes of today's world.
- Solving problems related to energy consumption and the need for sustainable development, in view of the theorem of conservation of mechanical energy and the most relevant thermodynamic processes, considering the analysis of the energy contained in a system, its properties and its manifestations.

**The Earth System**

- Interpretation of the characteristics of the stars of the solar system by relating them to the processes that took place during the origin of the Universe.
- Discussion on the possibility of life on other planets incorporating the hypotheses of the origin of life on Earth.
- Exemplification of the relationships between the community of organisms and the characteristics of the environment of natural systems. The case of living beings in soil formation.
- Analysis of the structure and dynamics of the geosphere, in view of plate tectonics and the resulting geological processes and risks.
- Analysis of the functions and dynamics of the Earth's fluid layers, their interaction with the Earth's surface and the resulting geological risks.
- Analysis of the basic classification of living beings and their adaptations to the physical characteristics of the environment in which they live.
- Solving problems on ecosystem dynamics: energy flows, matter cycles and trophic relationships.
- Research and reflection on the causes and consequences of the main environmental problems of our time (global warming, hole in the ozone layer, destruction of natural spaces, loss of biodiversity, etc.) and formulation of proposals for action.
- Argument and defense of the importance of the use of renewable resources against non-renewable ones, of their responsible exploitation, of renewable energies, of waste management and of the circular economy in the context of building a development model aligned with the objectives of sustainable development.
- Analysis of the relationships between environmental conservation, human health and the economic development of society from the perspective of sustainable development goals.
- Case study of a pandemic: causes, prevention and treatment of the most relevant infectious and non-infectious diseases, with special emphasis on the mechanism and importance of vaccines and the appropriate use of antibiotics.

**Biology for the 21st century**

- Differentiation of the main biomolecules on the basis of their basic structure and the functions they perform in living beings.
- Analysis and differentiation of the processes involved in the expression of genetic information and its relationship with the expression of a character, highlighting the central importance of the genetic code.
- Analysis of the procedure and assessment of the social and ethical implications of the use of the most relevant genetic engineering techniques (PCR, restriction enzymes, molecular cloning or CRISPR-CAS9) of gene therapies, stem cell transplantation and other biomedical technologies applied to human health and other fields of research and production.
- Application of strategies for solving problems of Mendelian inheritance, of one and two characters simultaneously and of the characters that are transmitted linked to the determination of genetic sex through the analysis of the probabilities of inheritance of alleles or manifestation of phenotypes.

**The forces that make us move**

- Application of the fundamental forces of nature in the description of the most relevant physical processes of the natural environment, such as electromagnetic phenomena, the movement of planets or nuclear processes.
- Analysis of structures in relation to physics, biology, geology or engineering using the laws of statics.
- Analysis and interpretation of the movement of an object based on the laws of mechanics, as a basis for explaining the behavior of an object in motion and its applications, for example, in road safety or technological development.
